A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAH dataset and benchmark study. The main text, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original dataset analyses and experiments on frame/video classification, zero-shot recognition and personalization, including results in Section 3 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds Video-FocalNet evaluations in Appendix I.2 and Table 17.

M1.justification: Dataset construction, annotation and existing recognition procedures are retained. Video-FocalNet is an additional existing-method benchmark, rather than a new proposed algorithm or component.

E1.justification: The BAH data, represented population and evaluated recognition/personalization tasks remain unchanged. Kinetics-400 appears as the source of Video-FocalNet's pretrained weights; the work does not report training or evaluating on that dataset itself. Localization is mentioned explicitly but receives no new evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 17 adds Video-FocalNet in tiny, small and base configurations to the video-level visual comparison. The APViT/ResNet comparators and the comparator sets for fusion, zero-shot inference and domain adaptation are retained.

E3.justification: The new Video-FocalNet experiment uses eight sampled face frames per video during training/testing, Kinetics-400 initialization, batch size 64 across four GPUs and 60 fine-tuning epochs. Section 2.4 also removes standalone positive-class F1 from the stated metrics, retaining AVGF1 and AP. Existing splits and benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The visual-input, context-length, modality/fusion, zero-shot prompt/context and demographic analyses retain their evidence. Video-FocalNet's additional model configurations extend the baseline comparison without introducing a distinct ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: Table 15 still reports means and standard deviations from five differently seeded repetitions; Table 24 retains participant-level means and standard deviations. No new uncertainty estimates, significance tests or repeated-run information accompany Video-FocalNet.

E6.justification: Table 17 adds Video-FocalNet AVGF1/AP results: tiny 0.5294/0.6545, small 0.5333/0.6558 and base 0.5663/0.6732. Existing scores remain unchanged, including APViT with context at 0.6134/0.3703. These are new-model results, not improvements to a retained method. A sentence about F1 versus context length is also removed while Figure 20 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: No theoretical results, formal assumptions, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations are added or revised. Existing definitions are retained; removing F1 from the metric list does not revise a mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the multimodal, participant-based A/H dataset and preliminary recognition, zero-shot and personalization benchmarks. v5 explicitly mentions localization and emphasizes domain adaptation in the conclusion, but the timestamp-based capabilities and personalization claims were already present in v3.

C2.justification: Appendix I.2 adds an interpretation favoring specialized video classification on average across metrics. Table 17 shows a metric-dependent advantage: Video-FocalNet base leads AP but trails APViT with context on AVGF1. Existing conflict-mechanism explanations and Appendix B limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v5 documents Video-FocalNet initialization and training details and changes the reported archive size from 10.3 GB to 9.6 GB in Figure 11. The main text emphasizes frame-extraction scripts and omits frames from the download-content list, although Figure 4 already shows frames and scripts in both versions. Actual file removal is therefore not established; access requirements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds the Kinetics and Video-FocalNets references supporting the new benchmark and extends the community-use account to ABAW 2026. Appendix A and the dataset's research positioning remain essentially unchanged. Updated publication metadata refers to existing cited works.

P1.justification: The main text receives grammatical, tense and terminology refinements, with several recast sentences and a rewritten conclusion. Publication headers change to ICLR 2026 and acknowledgements are added. The narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 6 and 19 gain an explicit Fusion Approach column; Table 17 gains Video-FocalNet rows and is resized and relocated. Other displays reflow, including grouping Tables 20–23 on one page. Existing scientific figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v5 makes the video-level benchmark more informative by adding a directly trained video classifier alongside the existing aggregation of frame predictions, with documented training details (Appendix I.2, Table 17). Language refinements and explicit fusion labels improve clarity. The gain is limited: existing limitations remain, and the new baseline's AP advantage does not extend to AVGF1 or come with uncertainty estimates.
